name: QA PR Learning
description: Lets QA learn from the persistent PR-comment log to surface team-specific review patterns during its own reviews.

learningEnabled.label: Learning Enabled
learningEnabled.description: Master switch for the PR-comment learning loop. When on, QA reads the comment log before each review and uses patterns found there to inform its own findings. When off, QA reviews are based solely on the in-session diff. On is the default — learning passively improves review quality without changing QA's interactive behavior.

logSourcePath.label: Log Source Path
logSourcePath.description: Path to the PR-comment log QA reads from. Empty defers to the log path configured in integration.bitbucket-pr-comments (the canonical source). Set explicitly only when QA should learn from a log other than the one the comments module writes (e.g. a curated team-wide log, an exported training set).

patternExtractionMode.label: Pattern Extraction Mode
patternExtractionMode.description: How QA distills patterns from the log. recurring-themes groups comments by topic (null checks, naming, error handling) and surfaces themes that appear in three or more comments. author-styles indexes comments by author and learns each reviewer's recurring concerns. literal-quotes surfaces specific phrasings from past comments as exemplars when QA is drafting verdict text. recurring-themes is the most useful default.

minLogEntriesToActivate.label: Min Log Entries To Activate
minLogEntriesToActivate.description: Minimum number of log entries required before the learning loop activates. Below this threshold, QA reverts to its non-learning behavior since the sample size is too small to produce reliable patterns. Default 10 is conservative; raise for stricter signal or lower for faster activation in new projects.

surfaceLearnedPatterns.label: Surface Learned Patterns
surfaceLearnedPatterns.description: When on, QA explicitly mentions learned patterns in its verdict ("This null check matches a recurring team pattern from CMMS-1234, CMMS-2456, CMMS-3567"). When off, QA uses the patterns internally to inform findings but does not cite them. On is useful for transparency and onboarding; off keeps verdicts cleaner for established teams.
